name: Other oral products (case-by-case)
anchor: sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant schedules with the Germany BVL 2017 TOOTHPASTE tier as the oral-mucosal anchor for formulated products, and Canada SOR/2018-83's mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling as the article anchor
native_basis: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total content, ug/kg as sold)
native_basis_label: finished oral-care product as placed on market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of product as sold (ug/kg). Not a dietary maximum level and not a migration/leachate value.
scope_note: Residual routing destination for oral-cavity products that do not fit rows 1-9, dispositioned case-by-case at the Step 0 category lock. Until that lock clears, the row publishes the strictest oral-cavity anchor available in this category — the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier — as the default floor for a FORMULATED product, taken as a disclosed read-across on every anchored cell because the exact form is by definition not yet determined. If the product routed here is an ARTICLE rather than a formulated product (a mouthguard, an appliance case, an intraoral device accessory), this row's values do NOT apply: the article contract used by the toothbrushes, floss, irrigator and tongue-scraper rows applies instead, and the row is re-derived at the Step 0 lock. Nothing certifies on this row without that lock.
basis_guard: ^(?!.*(colourant|colorant|colour additive|color additive|migration|leachate|food-contact|accessible part|candy as sold|as consumed|wet weight|toy))(?=.*(cosmetic|product as sold))
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor on a formulated oral row must be a FINISHED-COSMETIC (or finished oral-product) total-content instrument. The guard rejects three families that would otherwise conflate bases: colour-additive and ingredient purity specifications (21 CFR 73/74, the India permitted-colours entry), which cap one raw material and not the finished product; migration/leachate values (EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48 toy migration, food-contact migration), which measure release rather than content; and dietary maximum levels expressed as-consumed or wet weight. A basis failure resolves the cell to a GAP and fails the build rather than publishing a number in the wrong basis.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default), Category 20 Oral Care: a formulated oral product takes the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant maximum in its as-sold basis, with the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier read across to non-toothpaste oral-mucosal forms where it is stricter; an oral-care article takes the Canadian mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling and is otherwise held under component-level control. Species never replace totals, no ingredient purity specification anchors a finished-product cell, no migration value anchors a content cell, and no cell is occurrence-derived.

Pb.basis: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total lead content, ug/kg as sold) — read across from the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier
Pb.label: The exact cell is unregulated: no sovereign publishes a lead value for this product form. Germany BVL 2017's toothpaste tier (0.5 mg/kg) is the nearest applicable sovereign cell because it is the only sovereign lead value written for a product applied to the oral mucosa and partly swallowed, which is this form's exposure pattern. The directly applicable German general-cosmetic tier is 2 mg/kg; HMTc reads the stricter oral tier across rather than taking the looser general value, and discloses that choice here rather than presenting the number as direct regulatory alignment.
Pb.substantiation: This is the Category 15 precedent applied to its home matrix: the BVL toothpaste tier was read across to mucosal-contact products in the live Feminine Care standard on the reasoning that oral mucosa is the closest regulated analogue to other mucosa. Here the analogy is tighter still, because the target form is itself an oral-cavity product. The read-across moves the value DOWN from the directly applicable general-cosmetic tier (2000 to 500 ug/kg), so it cannot be characterised as a convenience selection.

Cd.basis: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total cadmium content, ug/kg as sold) — read across from the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier
Cd.label: The exact cell cannot be identified until the Step 0 lock fixes the product form, so no instrument can be said to regulate it directly. The Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier is read across as the strictest oral-cavity anchor available in this category; it is equal to the strictest general-cosmetic value for this analyte, so the read-across is not a stretch in either direction.
Cd.substantiation: Every anchored cell on this residual row is tagged read-across rather than regulatory alignment precisely because the form is undetermined. A Step 0 lock re-derives the row against the instrument family that matches the determined form before anything certifies.

tAs.basis: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total arsenic content, ug/kg as sold) — read across from the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier
tAs.label: The exact cell cannot be identified until the Step 0 lock fixes the product form, so no instrument can be said to regulate it directly. The Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier is read across as the strictest oral-cavity anchor available in this category; it is equal to the strictest general-cosmetic value for this analyte, so the read-across is not a stretch in either direction.
tAs.substantiation: Every anchored cell on this residual row is tagged read-across rather than regulatory alignment precisely because the form is undetermined. A Step 0 lock re-derives the row against the instrument family that matches the determined form before anything certifies.

iAs.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction of total arsenic. No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic content limit for any oral-care product: every sovereign arsenic value in the cosmetic instrument family (Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, China NMPA 2015, Korea MFDS, Taiwan MOHW, ASEAN and its national transpositions, Kenya KS 2937, EAEU TR CU 009/2011) is a TOTAL-arsenic value, and every sovereign inorganic-arsenic maximum level is scoped to rice, fish or fruit juice. The cell is therefore held under reflex speciation rather than given an invented ceiling; inorganic arsenic cannot exceed total arsenic by identity, so the published total-arsenic value (500 ug/kg) is its upper bound.
iAs.reference_method: Reflex HPLC-ICP-MS inorganic-arsenic speciation on any lot whose total-arsenic screen exceeds 50% of the published total-arsenic value. The inorganic fraction is held under ALARA against the tightest available context and any unexplained inorganic arsenic triggers supplier corrective action on the abrasive, clay, mineral-pigment or botanical-extract input that carries it.

tHg.label: The exact cell cannot be identified until the Step 0 lock fixes the product form, so no instrument can be said to regulate it directly. The Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier is read across as the strictest oral-cavity anchor available in this category; it is equal to the strictest general-cosmetic value for this analyte, so the read-across is not a stretch in either direction.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and bioaccumulates in fish muscle. A dentifrice, rinse, whitening or denture-care matrix has no methylating microbial community and no marine input; the mercury sources that reach this category are mineral-abrasive, clay and pigment impurities, which are inorganic. Methylmercury is a species of total mercury and cannot exceed it (MeHg <= tHg), so any mercury present is governed by and bounded by the published total-mercury ceiling of 100 ug/kg on this row.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold or CV-AAS. No separate methylmercury determination is required for an oral-care matrix; any lot above 50% of the total-mercury ceiling is investigated to its mercury source before release.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product. Every sovereign methylmercury maximum level in the register is scoped to fish and seafood. The applicable oral-care mercury instrument (Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier, 100 ug/kg) is a TOTAL-mercury value, and it bounds methylmercury by identity.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: Germany BVL 2017 (toothpaste and general-cosmetic tiers); US FDA 21 CFR 700.13; Washington State Toxics-Free Cosmetics Act; Health Canada Guidance on Heavy Metal Impurities in Cosmetics; China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards; Korea MFDS Notice 2024-9 and Notice 2025-63; Taiwan MOHW 2024; ASEAN Cosmetic Directive 2019 and the Indonesian (BPOM 16/2024), Malaysian (NPRA 2022), Singaporean (HSA 2024) and Thai transpositions; India Cosmetics Rules 2020; Kenya KS 2937:2021; EAEU TR CU 009/2011 — none sets a methylmercury value.

Ni.basis: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total nickel content, ug/kg as sold) — read across from the Korean residual finished-cosmetic nickel tier
Ni.source_scope: Cosmetic products other than eye makeup and color cosmetics
Ni.label: No sovereign names nickel in an oral-care product. Korea MFDS Notice 2024-9 Article 6(2) is the only instrument in the register that sets a finished-cosmetic nickel content limit at all, and it tiers it by product type: eye makeup 35 ug/g, colour cosmetics 30 ug/g, and all other cosmetics 10 ug/g. An oral-care product is neither eye makeup nor a colour cosmetic, so the residual 'other cosmetics' tier — the STRICTEST of the three — is the nearest applicable sovereign cell and is read across. HMTc does not use the looser makeup tiers.
Ni.substantiation: Nickel is a mucosal and contact sensitiser and reaches oral-care formulations through hydrated-silica and calcium-carbonate abrasives, mineral pigments, and stainless-steel process contact, so the cell must not be left without a ceiling where a sovereign anchor exists. The exact cell (nickel in a dentifrice, rinse, whitening system or denture-care product) is unregulated in every jurisdiction surveyed, which is why the value is published as a disclosed read-across tagged 'read-across' and not as regulatory alignment. Korea MFDS Notice No. 2025-63 restates the same three-tier nickel allowance at the same values; the 2024-9 row is named as the anchor because its register note reproduces the source unit without ambiguity.

Sn.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a tin content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product; the sovereign tin maximum levels in the register are canned-food and food-contact values written for tinplate migration into food and are a different basis entirely. Tin is additionally not a pure impurity in this category: stannous fluoride and stannous chloride are authorised anticaries and antigingivitis actives in dentifrices and mouthrinses, so a finished-product tin ceiling would be exceeded by design in a compliant stannous formulation and would be meaningless as a contaminant control. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control with a declaration reconciliation rather than declared not-material, because tin is unambiguously present at material levels in this category and an absence claim would be contradicted on its face.
Sn.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-tin analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold, reconciled against the batch record's declared stannous input. Tin in excess of the stoichiometric contribution of the declared stannous active, or any quantifiable tin in a product with no declared tin-bearing ingredient, triggers supplier corrective action under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule (ALARA against the tightest available context). No numeric ceiling is published.

Al.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an aluminium content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product. Aluminium is also frequently an intentional, declared functional ingredient in this category rather than a contaminant: hydrated alumina and aluminium oxide are conventional dentifrice abrasives, aluminium hydroxide is a common excipient, and aluminium lakes are the substrate of most permitted cosmetic colours. A finished-product aluminium ceiling would therefore be exceeded by design in a compliant alumina-abrasive formulation. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control with a declaration reconciliation rather than declared not-material, because aluminium is unambiguously present at material levels in this category.
Al.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-aluminium analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold (ICP-OES permitted where a high-alumina abrasive system saturates the ICP-MS working range), reconciled against the batch record's declared aluminium-bearing ingredients. Aluminium beyond the declared ingredient contribution triggers supplier corrective action on the abrasive, clay or pigment input under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule. No numeric ceiling is published.

Cr.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product; the only chromium values reachable from this category are the EU toy-migration figures, which are a leachate basis and are excluded by this row's basis guard. Total chromium is in any case a screen rather than a protective ceiling, since it is dominated by benign Cr(III) while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI). The cell is held under mandatory analytical control feeding the Cr(VI) reflex below, and no number is invented.
Cr.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-chromium analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold. Total chromium is used as the screen that triggers the Cr(VI) reflex; any result above the analytical reporting limit that cannot be traced to a declared Cr(III) pigment or to stainless-steel process contact is escalated to supplier corrective action.

Cr-VI.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product. Cr(VI) is deliberately NOT registered as a method-artifact not-material determination in this category: the method-artifact basis rests on Cr(VI) reducing to Cr(III) in the matrix, and oral-care matrices routinely contain oxidising systems — hydrogen peroxide and carbamide peroxide whiteners, sodium percarbonate and persulfate denture cleansers, peroxide-containing rinses — in which that reduction cannot be assumed. The cell is a control with a reflex speciation and a zero-tolerance disposition.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Reflex Cr(VI) speciation on any elevated total-chromium screen: alkaline extraction per EPA 3060A with IC-ICP-MS determination per EPA 6800, or EN 15192 for solid and paste matrices. Any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails the lot and blocks release pending supplier corrective action.
